neighbours.label: Word-final syllable piece 'la' (ola/ela/ila/ula) completing a name or word split by the tokenizer, e.g. Ang|ola, hyperb|ola, Renss|ela|er, Nic|ola; weaker on the standalone article ' la' and Arabic 'لا'
fire:
The delegation flew to Luanda after the long negotiations with Angola over the pipeline.
The talks resumed on Monday morning.
In the lecture notes, the focus of a hyperbola determines the shape of its two branches, as the teacher showed on the board.
Our new neighbor, Nicola Brandt, moved in last week and brought a plate of cookies to everyone on the street.
The study was led by Gabriela Montes and Ingela Strand, who presented their results at the Lund conference.
Reviews written by Camila Davila from Monterrey are now listed under the product page, sorted by date.
Another account holder, Akinola Bello, replied to the thread with a link to the quarterly report.
Sources say the team recovered the artifact near Lalibela, a town known for its rock-hewn churches.
El presidente habló a la prensa sobre la situación en la frontera, y la reunión terminó temprano.

The talks resumed on Monday morning.

notes: 10x pilot (concept-maps/tenx, random arm): label and 16 sentences written by a fresh Sonnet 5.5 subagent from a packet (card + all-pole band samples); no probes. An Opus gate checked rule-level items only (8 + 8, 0 overlap with census and probe text, near misses free of the declared trigger) and edited nothing. Labeller's note: Top examples are almost all the tokenizer piece 'ola/ela/ila/ula' ending a proper name or word (Angola, hyperbola, Nicola, Rensselaer); band samples add weaker firing on the Spanish/French article ' la' and Arabic 'لا'. Label is lexical and covers the strong cases but the weaker article firings are a separate, lower-activation mode.
